items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1959-06-02
items.q: Professor Welch then, he brought us to New Orleans and joined us in with the Silver Leaf Band under the leadership then of Albert Batiste.

ctx.x: Just about where was that in the Jefferson?

About one mile and a quarter out of the city limit. And we used to have to meet Professor Umphrey every Sunday morning about 9 o'clock. We had a little road cart. We'd carry him, flurry and two. And so the people that I wait for, they give us a place that we could have our practice, take our lessons, and might near every night while we was there playing and doing the best that we could. And so Professor Umphrey, I had to take him back in for it. And he advised me to buy a trombone. And I agreed to do so. And he…
Do you remember about, excuse me, what year that was about? Was that...

items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1961-04-07
items.q: my friend played cornet with us. In the Washington area, too, with Albert Batiste. He was the first cornet player with us.

ctx.x: He used to be our teacher, Frank Welch.

After I left off of Jefferson Powers, came to New Orleans, and my friend played cornet with us. In the Washington area, too, with Albert Batiste. He was the first cornet player with us. And his boy Joe played drum. Is Joe still alive? The old man, no, he's been there. I think Joe is the ... the ... the ... the ... the ... the ... the ... the ... the but I don't know whether he played music anymore or not. For that, his father and son, he used to play. But that's ... and he's a fine old musician, too. Old man,…
